Lara Croft: A Magical Journey

Angel Rittenburg — Expansion module, Summer 2021

Slide 1 of 8Title: A Magical Journey

The assignment

Design an expansion module for Lara Croft: a new story with its own levels.

Course
MMAN 40A · Introduction to Game Design
Instructor
Professor Phil Campbell
School
Berkeley City College, Summer 2021
Format
Game design pitch deck
Inspiration
"White Rabbit," Grace Slick (1967)

The story

Five stages, one hidden song

Synopsis. Lara enters a magical realm of reality to free the minds of young people around the world.

The beginning. While cataloging artifacts in the University of Avalon warehouse, Lara stumbles upon an old red upright piano that is missing some keys. Not knowing it's a magical piano, she begins to play her favorite Miles Davis album, Sketches of Spain, becomes hypnotized by the odd sound of the old piano, and nods off into a dreamy sleep.

The middle. Lara's mother comes to her in her dream and tells her she is about to begin a trip. She must choose a mode of transportation to reach her destination.

Tech City Challenge level. Lara must defeat megalomaniacal villains controlling the minds of young people.

Giant Lara level. Giant Lara must navigate a magical mushroom field, win a 3D chess game against men, and rescue rabbits from being hunted.

The finale. Lara wins all levels, frees the minds of millions of young people and returns to the Avalon University warehouse, where she is greeted by the artist Pink with a special performance.

The reveal. The whole journey is "White Rabbit" by Grace Slick.

Behind the story

From my presentation notes: Grace wrote "White Rabbit" on an old red upright piano missing a few keys, bought at a warehouse sale for $80. She worked out the tune after listening to Miles Davis's Sketches of Spain over and over, and she was riding the cable cars to her job modeling dresses at I. Magnin when she wrote it. The game's levels borrow the song's imagery: Alice growing tall, the men on the chessboard, and the mushroom. Pink has covered "White Rabbit," which is why she performs in the finale. This module later grew into my Fall 2022 "White Rabbit" final.
